senses.gloss:
चम् चम्, i. 1; ii. 5, Par. To sip.
 --With the prep. आ आ, base of the pres. etc., चाम,
 1. To sip water, Rām. 2, 52, 73.
 2. To rinse one's [] mouth, i. e. to make one's ablution, Man. 2, 61.
 3. To swallow figuratively, MBh. 5, 2978 (the horses swallowed the way, i. e. finished it very quickly).
 --Ptcple. of the pf. pass. आ-चान्त, in active sense, One who has rinsed his mouth, Man. 3, 251.
 --Ptcple. of the fut. pass., आ-चमनीय, n. Water for rinsing the mouth with, MBh. 3, 13662.
 --Causal, चामय, To cause to sip, Man. 5, 241.
 --With पर्या परि-आ, पर्याचान्त (viz. अन्न, food), One who has rinsed his mouth too early (without waiting the end of a meal), Man. 4, 212.
 --With समा सम्-आ, To make one's ablution, MBh. 13, 5063.
चमत्कार चमत्-कार (the latter part is कार, the former questionable), n. Surprise, Prab. 76, 15.

चमर चमर,
 I. m. Bos grunniens, Rām. 3, 49, 24.
 II. m. and n. The tail of the Bos grunniens, used to whisk off insects, flies, etc.; one of the insignia of royalty, MBh. 2, 1861; Vikr. d. 76.

चामर चामर, i. e. चमर + अ, n. The tail of the Bos grunniens, used to whisk off flies, and one of the insignia of royalty, Rājat. 5, 449: Megh. 36. Used also as an ornament on the heads of horses, Śāk. d. 8.
चमस चम् + अस, m. and n. A drinking vessel, Man. 5, 116.
चमू चमू, f. An army, Rām. 1, 74, 16, consisting of 729 elephants, 729 chariots, 2187 horses, and 3645 foot, MBh. 1, 292.
† चम्प् चम्प्, i. 10, Par. To go, v. r.

चम्पक चम्पक,
 I. m. A tree, Micelia champaca, Lin., Rām. 1, 17, 35.
 II. f. का. The name of a town, Hit. 27, 10.
 --Comp.

चम्पकवती चम्पकवती, i. e. चम्पक + वन्त् + ई, f.
 1. The name of a forest, Hit. 17, 13.
 2. The name of a town, 27, 10, v. r.
चम्पा चम्पा, f. The name of a town, Rām. 1, 17, 35.
† चम्ब् चम्ब्, i. 1, Par. To go.
चामुण्डा चामुण्डा, f. A name of Durgā, Mālat. 81, 6.
चमू- + नाथ चमू- + नाथ, m. a commander of an army, Bhāg. P. 4, 26, 3.
चमू- + पति चमू- + पति, m. the commander of an army.
चम्पक- + प्रभु चम्पक- + प्रभु, m. a proper name.
